task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 17, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper explainer answering why a falling wholesale produce index does not translate automatically into the same reduction at the grocery checkout.

facts.text: The Bramble Exchange reported its selected wholesale produce index 20% below a year earlier in July 2026.
The index tracks bulk market transactions in 40 produce categories, not a complete household grocery basket.
It excludes retail labor, store rent, refrigeration, packaging and losses from goods that cannot be sold.
At Spot Garden Market, a ten-kilogram tomato crate recently cost $24 instead of $30.
The shop's supplied handling records show about eight kilograms of saleable tomatoes from a typical crate in both comparison periods.
The retail price remained $4 per kilogram, giving $32 in potential sales from those eight kilograms if all were sold.
The difference between that potential $32 and the purchase cost widened from $2 to $8 per crate before retail overhead and unsold stock.
That difference is not the shop's net profit, and the record does not show that every crate sells completely.
Owner Keri Holt says refrigeration repairs and higher rent have absorbed part of the improved buying margin.
The shop has not supplied complete accounts independently establishing how much of the margin those costs absorbed.
A different grocer, Orchard Thread, remains on a three-month tomato supply contract at $28 a crate through August.
A lower spot-market quote does not automatically change that grocer's agreed contract price.
Holt said, "The crate got cheaper before the shop did."
Customer Oren Venn says he sees bulk-price headlines but shops across fresh food, cleaning products and packaged staples.
Venn said, "My basket is not the same basket as the number in the headline."
A local consumer group's ten-item retail basket fell from $48 to $47 over its comparison period, using a different product mix from the exchange index.
The consumer group reports listed shelf prices, not every household's actual purchases or promotional savings.
Neither comparison isolates a single cause for the gap between wholesale and retail prices.
The exchange operates before dawn in a former freight yard, while retail shops buy through several different supply arrangements.
The record contains no finding of illegal price coordination or proof that all retailers' profits moved together.

forbidden_additions: Every retail basket should mechanically fall 20% or $8 per crate is net profit
An audited explanation of all margin changes or proven price coordination
